questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted the destination to have a good university with interesting courses. I wanted a city with history and culture. I wanted a destination where I would meet people from all over the world- not just other Danish students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy. KU has most information on their website and everything else you get on mail. Uni of Edinburgh mostly communicate via mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
When I first arrived to my accommodation, there were multiple people handing out keys and information. An introduction meeting for exchange students was held by my student advisor, which was very helpful. During the entire semester, there were staff and other students in my dorm that were available to me if I had any questions or concerns. 
Uni of Edinburgh was great at communicating about all events and stuff happening via mail. The University also has an app for all events happening during the welcome week and semester. My dorm also had a Facebook group. 
The welcoming lasts an entire week and consists off a lot of different events across the whole University or just your school. You can choose to attend the events, but you're not obligated to. There are many opportunities to meet new people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The university has many student accommodations around the city.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I shared a kitchen with 23 other people. You have to bring/buy all your own cooking equipment. However, I believe the University has other accommodations with catered meals.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in Richmond Place. My view was amazing, I had a large bed and a nice desk. However, I did share bathrooms with at least 10 other people- all genders. We got toilet paper from the accommodation, but it would run out sometimes and you have to buy your own soap. I shared kitchen with 23 others. The kitchen wasn't always as clean and nice as I wished. However, each room has a separate cabinet in the kitchen with a lock, which was nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not receive an offer to live in an accommodation until 1-2 weeks before I left. Also I know of multiple people that moved into apartments when they first arrived, but then moved into student accommodation afterwards.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to go register at "international arrivals" at the school, at the library to pick up my student card and at the exchange student office. The University was good at making it clear what I had to do.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a student advisor and I also had staff at the accommodation I could ask.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Most classes fill up very quickly, however when you arrive at the Uni most people change courses within the first 1-2 weeks, and you have an opportunity here to have the courses you want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the emails from the Uni and attend the information events/meetings.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The topics of the courses were interesting. However, in my opinion the quality of the teaching is not as good as KU. My courses were graded on coursework I did throughout the semester and one course had a 10% participation mark as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are more lectures than seminars. I did not have to buy or read any books, just online articles.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Global Legal Systems, Street Law: public legal education in the community and EU Law Honours: Foundations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Global Legal Systems was interesting, but required a lot because it consisted of lectures twice a week, workshops once every second weak, 2 assignments throughout the semester and a moot court as the end of the semester. 
Street Law was not very legal. We did not really have classes or books. We just had to do one presentation on a legal topic at a charity center. 
EU Law was good, but still less "legal" than the courses at KU.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Cooking utensils, duvet and pillows. Remember that you do not get the entire Erasmus grant when on exchange. Some of it you receive after you get home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I thought I would have to spend money on books, which I did not. Also I think food is generally less expensive than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The University has a lot of student societies.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The gym has a lot of good classes. I also attended some of the events hosted by the Scandinavian society, which were good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city. Stockbridge is cozy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. The people are friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are very open, polite and easy to talk to.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is a very diverse city with students from all over the world. Do not get too caught up in the studies- enjoy the city and culture. Take the opportunities you are given to make friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: You grow from going outside of your comfort zone and meeting new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from everyone you know and sharing kitchen and bathroom with so many people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
